'''Jozef T. Devreese''' (born March 20, 1937; died November 1, 2023)<ref>https://blog.uantwerpen.be/collectief-geheugen/jozef-t-devreese/</ref> was a [[Belgians|Belgian]] scientist, with a long career in [[condensed matter physics]]. He was professor [[emeritus]] of [[theoretical physics]] at the [[University of Antwerp]]. 

== Academic career ==
Devreese graduated in 1960 from the [[Katholieke Universiteit Leuven]] where he received his [[PhD]] in science, group [[physics]] in 1964. From 1961 till 1966 he worked at the [[Solid State Physics]] Department of the Research Centre for Nuclear Energy (SCK-CEN) in [[Mol, Belgium|Mol]] ([[Belgium]]). In 1966 he started his work as lecturer and then full professor (from 1969) at the [[University of Antwerp]], where he founded the research group TFVS (Theoretische Fysica van de Vaste Stoffen). From 1977 he became also 'professor extraordinarius' at the [[Technische Universiteit Eindhoven]] (the [[Netherlands]]).

The results of his research are published in about 500 articles in international scientific journals. According to the [[Web of Knowledge]], there are more than 8300 citations of these publications in about 4300 citing papers.

== Cultural interests ==
As amateur of [[classical music]], he contributed to the realization on the Metzler organ<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.akc-orgel.be/akcv2/main.php?lang=en&tekstid=3|title=Antwerpse Kathedraalconcerten vzw}}</ref> in the [[Cathedral of Our Lady, Antwerp|Our Lady Cathedral]] in [[Antwerp]] (1993) and he was chairman (2000–2002) of the Flemish Institute for Organ Art (VIVO). He also contributed to the study<ref>J. T. Devreese, G. Vanden Berghe, ''Wonder en is gheen wonder. De geniale wereld van Simon Stevin 1548-1620'' (342 pp.), Davidsfonds, Leuven (2003)</ref><ref>J. T. Devreese, G. Vanden Berghe, ''Magic is No Magic. The Wonderful World of Simon Stevin'' (310 pp.), WIT Press, Ashurst, Southampton (2007)</ref>
of the work of [[Simon Stevin]] and to the promotion of the [[Dutch language]] and culture in the internationalized society.

== Distinctions / awards ==
* Three-annual prize for exact and natural sciences of the "Vlaamse Leergangen" of the [[KU Leuven|Katholieke Universiteit Leuven]] (1972).
* Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] (1990), Fellow of the [[European Physical Society]] (2006) and Fellow of the Institute of Physics, UK (2000).
* Doctor [[Honoris Causa]] of [[Moldova State University]] (1995), Honorary Member of the Academy of Sciences of the Republic of Moldova (2001).
* Member of the [[European Academy of Sciences and Arts]] (Salzburg, 2005).
